name: Jiantai
description: A star 226 parsecs away, 267 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: radius 266.935 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 8666.21 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.084) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: effective temperature 3411 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.057)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 92791: distance 225.734 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.041), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 226 parsecs away, 267 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 8,666 times the Sun's luminosity at 3,411 K, so 266.935 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 92791: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q
